LESSON: FICTION AND NON –FICTION 3.3.1 FICTION: THE NOVEL FROM KENYA

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: LITERATURE IN ENGLISH FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE
Strand: Strand 3
Topic 3.3: Fiction and Non –Fiction 3.3.1 Fiction: The Novel from Kenya
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 10

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Fiction and Non –Fiction 3.3.1 Fiction: The Novel from Kenya, part of Strand 3 in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 LITERATURE IN ENGLISH FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE.

Key inquiry question: How has history influenced prose fiction in Kenya? 2. Why is it key to pick out lessons learnt from a prose fiction?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Fiction and Non –Fiction 3.3.1 Fiction: The Novel from Kenya together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Creativity and imagination: This is enhanced as the learner embraces ideas that promote creativity when summarising

their findings on a tree diagram.

● Citizenship: This is nurtured when cultural and national identity skills are fostered as the learner interacts with

thematic concerns derived from the Kenyan setting.

Values:
● Social justice: This is enhanced as the learner accords peers equal opportunities when conducting a debate on how

history of Kenya has influenced the events and characters in the novel.

29

● Responsibility: This is nurtured as the learner exhibits self-initiative when teaming up with peers to form a book

reading club to read other novels from Kenya.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Nationalism: This is enhanced as the learner collaborates to promote social cohesion while they discuss the influence of

history and culture on fiction with peers.
